### Florida Corporate Income Tax Apportionment (Tax Years 2025 & 2026)

---

### 1. Apportionment Formula
* **Standard Formula:** Florida utilizes a three-factor formula with a double-weighted sales factor:
  * **Sales factor:** 50%
  * **Property factor:** 25%
  * **Payroll factor:** 25%
* **Zero or Insignificant Denominator Adjustments:**
  * If the sales denominator is zero or insignificant, the property and payroll factors are weighted at 50% each.
  * If either the property or payroll factor denominator is zero or insignificant, the remaining factor is weighted at $33\frac{1}{3}\%$, and the sales factor is weighted at $66\frac{2}{3}\%$.
  * If any two factor denominators are zero or insignificant, the remaining factor is weighted at 100%.
* **Single Sales Factor Exceptions:**
  * **Qualified Capital Expenditures:** Under Fla. Stat. § 220.153, taxpayers (excluding financial organizations) making qualified capital expenditures equal to or exceeding $250 million over a two-year period may apply and elect to apportion adjusted federal income solely by the sales factor.
  * **Citrus Processors:** Under Fla. Stat. § 220.151(3), eligible citrus processing companies may elect to apportion net income solely using the sales factor.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Florida Statutes § 220.15: http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.15.html
  * Florida Statutes § 220.153: http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.153.html
  * Florida Department of Revenue Corporate Income Tax Overview: https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx

---

### 2. Sourcing of Services and Intangibles
* **Rule:** **Cost of Performance (COP)**.
* **Standards:**
  * Gross receipts from services and other non-tangible personal property sales are attributed to Florida if the income-producing activity that gave rise to the receipts is performed wholly within Florida.
  * If the income-producing activity is performed both within and outside Florida, gross receipts are attributed to Florida only if the greater proportion of the income-producing activity is performed in Florida, based on costs of performance (F.A.C. Rule 12C-1.0155(2)(e), (2)(l)).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Florida Department of Revenue Technical Assistance Advisements (citing F.A.C. Rule 12C-1.0155):
    * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/rulings/Documents/08C1-002.pdf
    * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/rulings/Documents/17C1-004.pdf
  * Florida Statutes § 220.15(5): http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.15.html

---

### 3. Special Industry Apportionment Formulas
Florida provides specialized apportionment rules for the following industries:
* **Insurance Companies:** Apportioned using a single-factor direct premiums written fraction. 
  * *Numerator:* Direct premiums written for insurance upon properties and risks in Florida.
  * *Denominator:* Direct premiums written for insurance upon properties and risks everywhere.
  * *Reinsurance:* Specific rules apply where reinsurance is the company's principal source of premiums written (Fla. Stat. § 220.151(1)).
* **Transportation Services:** Apportioned using a revenue-miles fraction.
  * *Numerator:* Revenue miles in Florida.
  * *Denominator:* Revenue miles everywhere.
  * *Passenger/Freight:* Includes statutory formulas weighting passenger and freight revenue miles. Air and sea carriers compute Florida revenue miles over defined Florida boundaries/coordinates (Fla. Stat. § 220.151(2)).
  * *Pipelines:* Revenue mile defined as moving 1 barrel of oil, 1,000 cubic feet of gas, or a specified quantity of other substance 1 mile for consideration (Fla. Stat. § 220.151(2)(b)).
* **Citrus Processing Companies:** Allowed an election to apportion income solely using the sales factor (Fla. Stat. § 220.151(3)).
* **Financial Organizations:** Governed under standard three-factor apportionment, but subject to specialized statutory inclusions in the property and sales factors (e.g., intangible personal property, loans, interest, and fee receipts) (Fla. Stat. § 220.15(2)(c) & § 220.15(6)).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Source:**
  * Florida Statutes § 220.151: http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.151.html

---

### 4. Forms and Schedules Used to Compute Apportionment
* **Primary Corporate Return:** **Florida Form F-1120** (*Florida Corporate Income/Franchise Tax Return*).
  * **Schedule III** (*Apportionment of Adjusted Federal Income*):
    * **Schedule III-A:** Standard three-factor formula computation (Average value of property, Salaries/wages/commissions/compensation, and Sales).
    * **Schedule III-B:** Computation of average value of property (original cost).
    * **Schedule III-C:** Sales factor calculation.
    * **Schedule III-D:** Special apportionment fractions (Line 1 for insurance companies; Line 2 for transportation services).
* **Partnership Information Return:** **Form F-1065**, Part III (*Apportionment Information*) and Part IV (*Apportionment of Partners' Share*).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Florida Form F-1120: https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/f1120.pdf
  * Florida Form F-1120 Instructions: https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/f1120n.pdf

### 1. Corporate Income / Franchise Tax Nexus & Bright-Line Thresholds

* **Nexus Standard:** Florida imposes corporate income/franchise tax on all corporations for the privilege of conducting business, deriving income, or existing within Florida. Activities that establish nexus include:
  * Having employees, agents, or independent contractors conducting sales or other business activities in Florida;
  * Maintaining an office or other place of business in Florida;
  * Assembling, installing, servicing, or repairing products in Florida;
  * Owning, renting, or leasing real property or tangible personal property in Florida;
  * Delivering goods to Florida customers using company-owned or leased vehicles;
  * Holding a partnership interest in a partnership doing business, deriving income, or existing in Florida (Fla. Admin. Code R. 12C-1.011(1)(v));
  * Selling or licensing intangible property for use in Florida (e.g., trademarks, patents) (Fla. Admin. Code R. 12C-1.011(1)(p)).
* **Economic Nexus / Bright-Line Factor Presence Threshold:** Not found. Florida statutes and administrative rules do not provide a bright-line factor presence nexus standard or a specific dollar-amount economic nexus threshold for corporate income tax.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
  * Florida Department of Revenue (Corporate Income Tax): `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx`
  * Florida Department of Revenue (Out-of-State Businesses): `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/outofstate.aspx`
  * Florida Statutes § 220.11: `https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.11.html`

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold & Measurement Period (Sales Tax)

* **Sales Threshold:** Total taxable remote sales into Florida in excess of **$100,000** (Fla. Stat. § 212.0596(1)(b)).
* **Transaction Count:** None. Florida law specifies **any number** of taxable remote sales (no transaction minimum).
* **Measurement Period:** The **previous calendar year** (Fla. Stat. § 212.0596(1)(b)).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (effective July 1, 2021; unchanged for 2025 and 2026).
* **Official URLs:**
  * Florida Statutes § 212.0596: `https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0212/Sections/0212.0596.html`
  * Florida Department of Revenue (Sales and Use Tax): `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/salestax.aspx`
  * Florida Department of Revenue TIP No. 21A01-03: `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/documents/tip21a01-03.pdf`

---

### 3. State Position on Public Law 86-272 Protection

* **Recognition and Incorporation:** Florida explicitly incorporates Public Law 86-272 (15 U.S.C. §§ 381–384) by reference into its administrative rules (Fla. Admin. Code R. 12C-1.0511(2)). 
* **Scope of Protection:** 
  * A business is protected from Florida corporate income tax if its Florida activity is limited strictly to the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property, provided the orders are sent outside Florida for approval or rejection and filled by shipment or delivery from a point outside Florida by mail or common carrier.
  * Having sales representatives in Florida carry and demonstrate samples or use company cars does not by itself exceed protection (Fla. Admin. Code R. 12C-1.011(2)).
  * Activities exceeding solicitation (unless *de minimis* under *Wisconsin Department of Revenue v. William Wrigley, Jr., Co.*)—such as in-state repair/servicing, demonstrating customer-owned goods, technical consulting, administrative remote employees, or independent contractors approving orders—eliminate P.L. 86-272 immunity and create corporate income tax nexus (Fla. Admin. Code R. 12C-1.011(1)(k), (l)).
* **MTC Revised Internet Activity Guidance:** Not found. The Florida Department of Revenue has not issued published rules or official guidance adopting the Multistate Tax Commission's 2021 revised interpretations regarding internet activities under P.L. 86-272.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
  * Florida Department of Revenue (Out-of-State Businesses): `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/outofstate.aspx`
  * Florida Department of Revenue Technical Assistance Advisement 11C1-006: `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/legal_treatments/Documents/11C1-006.pdf`
  * Florida Department of Revenue Technical Assistance Advisement 10C1-009: `https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/legal_treatments/Documents/10C1-009.pdf`

notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax
* **Rate / Brackets:** Florida does not impose an individual (personal) income tax.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/new_resident.aspx
  * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/tax_rates.aspx

---

### 2. Corporate Income / Franchise Tax
* **Rate:** 
  * **General Rate:** **5.5%** on Florida net income (for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2022).
  * **Alternative Minimum Rate:** **3.3%** for taxpayers determining taxable income under section 220.13(2)(k), F.S. (subject to federal Alternative Minimum Tax).
  * **Exemption:** An exemption of up to **$50,000** of net income is allowed in computing tax liability.
* **Minimum Tax:** Florida does not impose a fixed dollar minimum corporate income/franchise tax.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx
  * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/tax_rates.aspx
  * http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.11.html
  * http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=&URL=0200-0299/0220/Sections/0220.14.html

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax
* **State Rate:** **6%** general rate. 
  * *Specific statutory state rate exceptions:* Retail sales of new mobile homes: **3%**; amusement machine receipts: **4%**; electricity: **6.95%**.
* **Local Option Surtaxes:** Florida counties may levy a local discretionary sales surtax (county tax) in addition to the state sales and use tax. The surtax applies to transactions delivered into a county that imposes it (for most transactions, the surtax applies only to the first $5,000 of a taxable sale).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (state base rate remains unchanged; specific county surtax rates adjust locally by calendar year).
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/sales_tax.aspx

---

### 4. Gross Receipts and Notable Business Taxes
* **Gross Receipts Tax on Utility Services:** 
  * Imposed at a rate of **2.5%** on the sale, delivery, or transportation of natural gas, manufactured gas (excluding LP gas), or electricity to retail consumers in Florida.
  * *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (rate unchanged; administrative index prices are updated annually on July 1).
  * *Official URL:* https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/grt.aspx
* **Communications Services Tax (CST):**
  * Imposed on telecommunications, video, and audio signals. 
  * Total state CST rate is **7.44%** (comprising **4.92%** state tax + **2.52%** gross receipts tax [2.37% + 0.15%]).
  * Direct-to-home satellite service total rate is **11.44%** (**9.07%** state + **2.37%** gross receipts tax).
  * Municipalities and charter counties impose an additional local CST rate.
  * *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
  * *Official URL:* https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/cst.aspx
* **Gross Receipts Tax on Dry-Cleaning Facilities:**
  * Imposed at a rate of **2%** on all gross receipts/charges by dry-cleaning and dry drop-off facilities for dry-cleaning and laundering services.
  * *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
  * *Official URL:* https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/drycleaning.aspx

notes:
### Individual Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **Fact:** Florida does not impose a personal income tax (authorized by Article VII, Section 5 of the Florida Constitution). Consequently, there are no individual return filing requirements, no calendar-year filing due dates, and no extension procedures for individuals.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** [https://floridarevenue.com/faq/Pages/search.aspx](https://floridarevenue.com/faq/Pages/search.aspx) (FAQ: *Do I have to file a personal income tax return in Florida?*)

---

### Corporate and Pass-Through Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **Corporate Income Tax (Form F-1120 / F-1120A):**
  * **Due Date:** For calendar-year filers, the return is due the later of:
    1. On or before the 1st day of the 5th month following the close of the taxable year (May 1); or
    2. The 15th day following the due date, without extension, for filing the related federal return.
    *(If the due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal/state holiday, filing is timely if postmarked on the next business day).*
  * **Extensions:** Corporations may request a 6-month extension (extending a calendar-year return due date to November 1) by filing Florida Form F-7004 and paying 100% of tentative tax due on or before the original return due date. A federal extension alone does not extend a Florida return.
  * *Fiscal Year Note (June 30 Year-End):* For tax years beginning before January 1, 2026, returns are due on or before the 1st day of the 4th month (October 1). For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, the due date changes to the 1st day of the 5th month (November 1).
* **Pass-Through Entities (Form F-1065):**
  * **Filing Requirement:** An LLC or partnership doing business, earning income, or existing in Florida must file Form F-1065 only if one or more of its owners/partners is a corporation.
  * **Due Date:** Due on or before the 1st day of the 4th month following the close of the taxable year (April 1 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extensions:** An extension of 6 months (to the 1st day of the 10th month / October 1 for calendar filers) is obtained by submitting Florida Form F-7004 on or before the original return due date. Only one extension is permitted.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (the June 30 corporate fiscal year due date changes for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026; calendar-year rules remain unchanged).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * [https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx)
  * [https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/cit/duedates](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/cit/duedates)

---

### Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)
* **Fact:** Not found. Florida does not impose an individual personal income tax and has not enacted an elective pass-through entity tax regime or PTE tax rate.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** Not found ([Chapter 220, Florida Statutes](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/Chapter220) / [https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx)).

---

### Composite or Group Nonresident Returns for Pass-Through Entities
* **Fact:** Not found. Because Florida imposes no personal income tax on individuals, pass-through entities do not file composite or group income tax returns for nonresident individual owners. Any corporate partner must independently file its own Florida corporate income tax return (Form F-1120).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** Not found ([Chapter 220, Florida Statutes](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/Chapter220) / [https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx)).

---

### Estimated Tax Payment Requirements and Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Throughs
* **Pass-Through Entity Estimated Taxes & Nonresident Withholding:**
  * **Fact:** Not found / Not required. Pass-through entities have no entity-level estimated tax payment requirement, and there is no state income tax withholding required on nonresident partners/members.
* **Corporate Estimated Tax Requirements:**
  * **Threshold:** Every corporation or entity subject to tax under Chapter 220, Florida Statutes, must declare and pay estimated tax if its annual Florida tax liability is expected to exceed $2,500.
  * **Installment Schedule (Calendar-Year Filers):** Paid in four equal installments of 25% (0.25) due on or before:
    * Installment 1: Last day of the 5th month (May 31)
    * Installment 2: Last day of the 6th month (June 30)
    * Installment 3: Last day of the 9th month (September 30)
    * Installment 4: Last day of the taxable year (December 31)
    *(For tax years ending June 30, installments are due on or before the last day of the 4th, 6th, and 9th months, and the last day of the tax year).*
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * [https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx)
  * [https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/Chapter220](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/Chapter220) (Sections 220.24 and 220.33, F.S.)

---

### Main Return Forms
* **Individual Return Forms:** None (no individual income tax returns exist in Florida).
* **Corporate Forms:**
  * **Form F-1120:** Florida Corporate Income/Franchise Tax Return
  * **Form F-1120A:** Florida Corporate Short Form Income Tax Return
  * **Form F-1120ES:** Declaration/Installment of Florida Estimated Income/Franchise Tax
  * **Form F-7004:** Florida Tentative Income/Franchise Tax Return and Application for Extension of Time to File Return
* **Pass-Through Entity Forms:**
  * **Form F-1065:** Florida Partnership Information Return (used by partnerships/LLCs with corporate partners)
  * **Form F-7004:** Application for Extension of Time to File Form F-1065
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
  * [https://floridarevenue.com/forms](https://floridarevenue.com/forms) (Corporate Income Tax section)
  * [https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/corporate.aspx)
